themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street conditions complaints spiked to 45 this week versus a baseline of 8.1 per week (454% increase, z-score 7.51), suggesting rapid deterioration in road quality across Crown Heights/Prospect Heights that warrants immediate investigation into whether potholes, cracking, or subsurface issues are concentrated in specific blocks.
evidence: 45 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (454% spike)
Z-score of 7.51 indicates statistically rare event
Concurrent spike in illegal dumping (14 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.5 avg) suggests debris or material accumulation on streets
reporting_angles: Map specific blocks reporting street damage to identify whether pothole concentration is in one area (e.g., near transit hub, aging infrastructure zone)
Interview NYC DOT to determine if they've identified the cause (water main breaks, freeze-thaw cycles, heavy construction traffic) and response timeline

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints jumped to 14 this week against a baseline of 4.5 per week (211% increase, z-score 5.48), representing a sharp acceleration in environmental violations that converges with street condition complaints and repeating community board requests for enhanced sanitation.
evidence: 14 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.5 weekly average (211% spike, z-score 5.48)
Community Board has filed repeated 'other cleaning requests' with Sanitation Department, indicating chronic resource shortfall
Spatial correlation: same week as street condition crisis suggests dumping may be both cause and symptom of neighborhood neglect
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine enforcement response: are dumping sites being cleared, and how many violations have been issued to repeat dumpers?
Canvass blocks with highest 311 complaint density to photograph conditions and document whether illegal dumping aligns with poor street maintenance

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints reached 3 last week versus a baseline of 0.5 per week (500% increase, z-score 3.54), a potential public health signal warranting urgent review of which buildings triggered reports and whether demolition or renovation permits filed this quarter may have disturbed asbestos-containing materials.
evidence: 3 asbestos complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score 3.54)
479 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (302 alterations, 13 full demolitions) — permits that can disturb asbestos if not properly managed
Concurrent spike in indoor air quality complaints (13 two weeks ago vs. 2.9 avg, 352% increase) may indicate airborne hazard concerns from construction
reporting_angles: Obtain NYC Department of Environmental Protection asbestos violation records for the district in the past 30 days; cross-reference against DOB demolition and alteration permits to identify which projects may have triggered exposures
Interview community residents about timing of complaints relative to nearby construction activity; determine if asbestos reports cluster geographically

themes_detail.label: Emergency Response Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Emergency Response Team (ERT) complaints jumped to 4 this week from a baseline of 1.0 per week (300% increase, z-score 4.24), a sharp spike in incidents severe enough to trigger police/emergency dispatch that deserves investigation into whether a specific public safety crisis has emerged.
evidence: 4 ERT complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 4.24)
No recent community board agendas or council constituent cases available to contextualize complaint type
311 complaint category alone does not specify ERT incident type (mental health crisis, violence, disorder, etc.)
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with NYPD to obtain ERT dispatch logs and call types for Crown Heights/Prospect Heights this week; determine whether incidents are concentrated in specific locations or time periods
Contact NYPD 77th Precinct to ask what emergency calls prompted ERT response and whether a public safety trend is emerging

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 13 two weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.9 per week (352% increase, z-score 5.74), coinciding with asbestos and street deterioration signals and potentially indicating construction-related dust, mold, or other environmental hazards affecting indoor conditions across the district.
evidence: 13 indoor air quality complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 2.9 weekly baseline (352% spike, z-score 5.74)
Concurrent asbestos spike and 479 DOB building permits suggest construction dust/debris may be source
Heat/hot water complaints remain the highest category (3788 over 90 days), indicating building system issues that can contribute to mold and air quality problems
reporting_angles: Survey residents who filed indoor air quality complaints to identify common symptoms (respiratory, mold odors, dust) and building types affected
Cross-reference indoor air quality and asbestos complaints geographically to determine if both cluster around specific construction sites
